prerequisites: The student is assumed to have acquired general knowledge of technical activities in the field of computer science.

learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge to organize, plan, and manage a project, based on their existing technical knowledge.
Enable students to prepare project-related documents and process them, including the contracting phase.
Familiarize students with the most commonly used standards for project management.
Ability to plan, conceive, deploy, and direct IT projects, services, and systems in all areas, leading their implementation and continuous improvement.
Ability to plan, conceive, deploy, and direct IT projects, services, and systems in all areas, assessing their economic and social impact.
Ability to understand the importance of negotiation, effective work habits, leadership, and communication skills in all software development environments.
Ability to prepare the technical specifications for an IT installation that complies with current standards and regulations.
Knowledge of IT regulations and legislation at national, European, and international levels.
Know the types of projects and the methodologies and standards for their planning, control, and management.
Contract and bid for projects in compliance with regulations.
Know and apply techniques that ensure project management quality.

syllabus_topics: The project: concept, types and characteristics. Project lifecycle.
Human resource management for the project.
Methodologies and standards for project management. Agile methodologies.
Documentation for the final degree project. Project presentations.
Group practical work: a project from conception to contract documentation and other associated documentation.
Individual practical work with planning tools (Microsoft Project).

assessment_methods.method: Group work, contribution tracking, memory submission, oral presentation and final defense
Final in-person knowledge test (Test and/or short questions, application cases, problem solving)

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, each of the three parts (group work, individual activities, and in-person test) must be passed with a minimum grade of 5 out of 10. The final grade is calculated as: 0.4 * Group Work + 0.1 * Individual Work + 0.5 * In-person Test. For the extraordinary call, approved work from the ordinary call will be considered; otherwise, an equivalent individual assignment will replace it. A knowledge test will also be conducted. The final grade for the extraordinary call is: 0.6 * In-person Test + 0.4 * Assignments Grade, requiring at least 5 in each part. For differentiated assessment, students are exempt from mandatory attendance to practices. Their mastery of concepts will be assessed via an exam (60% of final grade) and an individual assignment similar to course work, defended before a tribunal (40% of final grade), with at least 5 in each part.
